Low knowledge retention: Standard safety lecture metrics show that over 65% of regulatory information fade from memory within 14 days without high-immersion scenario drill reinforcement.
Reliance on user to describe process upfront: The conversational agent cannot create a process chart unless the user initiates a comprehensive description of workflow steps.
No formal evaluation of TO-BE model quality: The framework suggests process improvements but lacks a quantitative metrics suite to check the validity of new models.
Traditional Methods Difficult to Meet Demand: Manual categorization of unstructured text problem descriptions cannot process the thousands of quality issues generated monthly across sites.

Dispersion and distraction (cell phone use and conversations): Trainees in traditional group classroom lectures frequently lose focus due to side chat or mobile application alerts, interrupting skill acquisition.
Static Spot Projection Constraint: The spatial user-interface layout docks textual alerts to fixed spatial coordinates, forcing workers to repeatedly turn away from their active field.
Monolithic view of knowledge / rigidity: Traditional structural relational databases force fluid, context-dependent site entities into rigid tabular rows, filtering out key nuances.
Fixed size and flatness of traditional SOM: Classical Self-Organizing Maps utilize a static structural grid topology, preventing the network from adapting to dynamic knowledge domains.
Unstructured external data data-validity concerns: A large percentage of knowledge artifacts posted on corporate social threads contain unverified advice and outdated rule-of-thumb heuristics.
Data quality concerns: User-generated wiki threads often display poor organization, unformatted syntax, and factual skews that mislead junior engineers.
Ad hoc usage: Without structural workflow integration, professional platform use degenerates into informal, ad-hoc interactions that escape tracking.
Low efficiency in analyzing and disposing of quality issues: Traditional text queries return thousands of unorganized historical rows, requiring engineers to spend days tracking down related defects.
Inconvenient information retrieval: Siloed cross-departmental documentation databases force operators to manually run multiple individual system search lookups.
Repeatedly sort out and extract knowledge: Because historical repair files lack structured tags, engineering teams must repeatedly review and extract core concepts manually.
Insufficient knowledge sharing: The current organizational architecture allows valuable project quality solutions to remain locked inside regional division folders."

column2: Inconsistent or malformed XML generation: gpt-4o sometimes produced invalid syntax... resulting in execution errors when parsed by standard engine setups.
Incomplete Data: Missing attributes within standard construction failure logs restrict the downstream accuracy of programmatic semantic graph ingestion engines.
Missing Measurement Parameters: Many quality inspect logs omit key spatial measurements and load parameters, rendering structural failure records analytically blind.
Incomplete Historical Records: Legacy quality tracking sheets from 2018 to 2021 suffer from massive text gaps, missing descriptions, and unarchived repair follow-ups.
Data Blank: The presence of data blanks within official site non-conformance spreadsheets breaks the logical dependency chain during parsing steps.
Information Blind Area: Subcontractor handovers represent an information blind area where quality inspection actions escape formal enterprise tracking systems.
Gap between User Expression and Standard Terms: Field operators query knowledge graphs using colloquial slang, causing search failures due to strict vocabulary indexing boundaries."
Lack of clear position indicator on physical component: Trainees frequently struggle to find exact bolt locations because the physical casing lacks high-contrast visual markers or positional labels.
Jittery visualization of holes on board: Environmental lighting glare caused the AR tracker to lose focus, creating a jittery visualization of alignment holes.
Lack of spatial visualization: Traditional flat diagrams cannot accurately project structural depth, making complex structural alignment tasks hard to learn.
Jittery visualization: The virtual annotations trembled when the user moved their head quickly, causing spatial tracking errors.
Inability to detect assembly errors: The application guides steps linearly but does not actively evaluate whether the operator placed a physical component incorrectly.
Lack of Automated Performance Feedback: The wearable smart glasses system projects visual directions statically but cannot systematically verify if a screw was torqued to target limits.
Small Text Size: Using tiny pixel-font dimensions on optical see-through waveguides forces operators to squint, inducing rapid eye strain and blurring.
Difficulty interpreting 2D drawings: Trainees frequently struggle to map flat blueprint vectors onto complex physical spatial components accurately.
Limited robot hardware capacity: Deploying heavy transformer-based embedding parsing directly onto embedded robotic controllers causes rapid memory exhaustion and processing stalls.
Inaccurate or low-quality onboard sensors: Low-cost RGB-D cameras generate significant point cloud noise under outdoor construction sunlight, distorting semantic obstacle mapping.
Hardware constraints of humanoid robots: Embedded mobile edge platforms possess severe computing, RAM, and thermal thresholds that conflict with deep spatial graph traversals."
Inefficiency of manual communication and paper-based steps: Manual methods of capturing process details are slow and error-prone, requiring several follow-up iterations."
Repeated use of shuffled questions potential bias: Re-using identical question pools across pre- and post-tests introduces a high risk of memory bias among trainees.
response bias: Relying on descriptive questionnaires introduces subjective distortion, as participants align answers with perceived social desirability."
